newsitem.title: USA: Hollywood Entertainment to sell $200 mln junk debt.
newsitem.headline: Hollywood Entertainment to sell $200 mln junk debt.

text.p: Hollwood Entertainment Corp announced on Monday that it plans to sell $200 million in senior subordinated notes due 2004 in a 144a private placement.
Proceeds from the offering will be used to repay a $101.0 million revolving credit facility, to fund expansion and for working capital and other general corporate purposes, the company said.
Market sources said the deal will be lead-managed by Montgomery Securities, a San Francisco-based securities firm.
Hollywood Entertainment owns and operates 661 video retail superstores in 33 states.
The offering will be one of the first to be lead-managed by Montgomery, which is a recent entrant into the junk bond underwriting business.
Montgomery will also lead-manage a $200 million junk bond offering from Signature Resorts Inc, which was announced last week, market sources said.
The roadshows for both offering will begin this Friday. Both deals are expected to be priced in the first week of August, they said.
NationsBank Corp of Charlotte, North Carolina, has agreed to acquire Montgomery for $1.2 billion.
